Let the roots be \(r_1,\dots,r_n\), and let \(e_k\) be their elementary symmetric sums. By Vieta,
\[
e_{n-2}=(-1)^{n-2}\lambda W,\quad
e_{n-1}=(-1)^{n-1}\lambda AB,\quad
e_n=(-1)^n\lambda.
\]
If \(\lambda\ne 0\), then \(e_n\ne0\). Put \(y_i=1/r_i\). Then
\[
\frac{e_{n-1}}{e_n}=\sum_{i=1}^n y_i,\qquad 
\frac{e_{n-2}}{e_n}=\sum_{i<j}y_i y_j.
\]
By Cauchy,
\[
\left(\sum y_i\right)^2\le n\sum y_i^2,
\]
which is equivalent to
\[
\left(\sum y_i\right)^2\ge \frac{2n}{n-1}\sum_{i<j}y_i y_j.
\]
Thus
\[
e_{n-1}^2\ge \frac{2n}{n-1}e_{n-2}e_n.
\]
Substituting the Vieta expressions gives
\[
\lambda^2 A^2B^2\ge \frac{2n}{n-1}\lambda^2 W.
\]
Since \(\lambda\ne0\),
\[
A^2B^2\ge \frac{2n}{n-1}W.
\]

On the other hand, the vectors
\[
(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n,|A|),\qquad (\beta_1,\dots,\beta_n,|B|)
\]
both have norm \(1\). Hence by Cauchy,
\[
\sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_j\beta_j+|AB|\le 1,
\]
so
\[
1-\sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_j\beta_j\ge |AB|.
\]
Squaring gives
\[
2W=\left(1-\sum_{j=1}^n \alpha_j\beta_j\right)^2\ge A^2B^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{2n}{n-1}W\le A^2B^2\le 2W.
\]
But \(n\ge4\) implies \(\frac{2n}{n-1}>2\), and \(W>0\), a contradiction. Hence \(\lambda\ne0\) is impossible.

For \(\lambda=0\), the equation becomes \(x^n=0\), which has only real roots.

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
